items.answer: No. The best baseline was Attr. IG at −2.17%, Act. and Attr. produced no circuit, and the rest were at 0%.
rubric: Answers no.
Notes the best baseline was Attr. IG at about −2% and Act./Attr. cells are empty.

items.question: On Llama IOI, did any baseline produce an accuracy drop larger than 10%?
items.answer: Yes. Act. reached −59.17%, although with a large standard deviation (±41.90).
rubric: Answers yes.
Identifies Act. with about −59% accuracy drop.

items.question: If S³martCirc had labelled head 10.10 passthrough, would that contradict the human-verified Acronym circuit under the Figure 1 mapping?
items.answer: No. Prior work shows 10.10 can act as either a Bridge head or a Letter Mover. Bridge maps to passthrough, so a passthrough label would still be consistent.
rubric: Answers no.
Reasons that 10.10 can act as a Bridge head, which maps to passthrough.

items.question: If S³martCirc had labelled head 11.4 passthrough, would that contradict the human-verified Acronym circuit under the Figure 1 mapping?
items.answer: Yes. 11.4 is a Letter Mover, and letter mover heads map to the functional role, so a passthrough label would be a mismatch.
rubric: Answers yes.
Reasons that 11.4 is a Letter Mover, which maps to functional.

items.question: On Llama Acronym, was S³martCirc's circuit smaller than Attr. IG's?
items.answer: Yes. S³martCirc averaged 47.33 nodes against Attr. IG's 54.67.
rubric: Answers yes.
Cites 47.33 versus 54.67 nodes.

items.question: On Llama IOI, was S³martCirc's circuit smaller than Act.'s?
items.answer: No. S³martCirc averaged 35 nodes, while Act. averaged 13.
rubric: Answers no.
Cites 35 versus 13 nodes.

items.question: A team wants to recover as much of Wang et al.'s IOI circuit in GPT-2 as possible while spending the least compute. Which method does the paper's evidence favour, and why?
items.answer: S³martCirc. Its IOI recovery is matched only by Act., and the other baselines recover much less. It also ran in about 264 s on GPT-2 IOI versus about 7,944 s for Act., roughly 30 times faster.
rubric: Recommends S³martCirc.
Notes that only Act. has comparable recovery, and Act. is about 30× slower (≈264 s vs ≈7,944 s).

items.question: Two candidates in N_i face the same sparsity pressure; one has FI = 1.05 and the other FI = 6. Which is more likely to remain in the circuit through the classification stage, and why?
items.answer: The FI = 6 node. L_class's push to raise its c_f has magnitude 6. For FI near 1 both pushes, FI and 1/FI, are about 1, the weakest possible support, so the sparsity term is more likely to prune that node.
rubric: Chooses the FI = 6 node.
Explains that L_class's push is weakest when FI is near 1 (gradient magnitude max(FI, 1/FI)), so sparsity dominates for that node.

items.question: In a new task's circuit, a head writes into the residual stream information about an earlier occurrence of the current token, without otherwise altering it. Under the paper's dichotomy, which role should it be expected to have, and why?
items.answer: Passthrough. It is analogous to the previous token heads that Figure 1 maps to passthrough: it relocates information about another position with minimal transformation.
rubric: Predicts passthrough.
Draws the analogy to previous token heads, which relocate information and are mapped to passthrough.

items.question: On Qwen IOI, a team wants the smallest circuit whose ablation completely breaks the task. Should they choose Act., which gives the smallest circuit, or S³martCirc, and why?
items.answer: S³martCirc. Act.'s 12-node circuit causes only a −33% drop, and that comes from a single run. S³martCirc's 16.33-node circuit gives −100% with zero variance across three runs, so it is the smallest circuit that meets the goal.
rubric: Recommends S³martCirc.
Notes that Act.'s smaller circuit only reaches −33% (single run), whereas S³martCirc reaches −100% at about 16 nodes.

items.question: A team builds a variant pipeline that keeps only functional nodes as the circuit and treats passthrough nodes as unimportant. Is this sound given the paper's findings, and why?
items.answer: No. In the paper, passthrough nodes are important circuit components: S-inhibition, previous token and bridge heads, and S³martCirc's own Acronym passthrough nodes 1.0 and 8.11. Importance (c_p + c_f vs c_u) is separate from role, so dropping passthrough nodes would omit critical components.
rubric: Says it is not sound.
Explains that passthrough nodes (e.g., S-inhibition, previous token, bridge heads, or 1.0/8.11) are part of verified circuits, and that role is distinct from importance.

items.question: If S³martCirc-IF had matched the full method on both tasks, which conclusion of the ablation study would lose its support?
items.answer: The conclusion that alternating, bidirectional optimization is needed beyond using functional interpretation as a prior. The paper argues that IF is 'insufficient without the alternating training', and that argument rests on IF underperforming the full method.
rubric: Identifies the claim that alternating/bidirectional training is necessary (beyond functional interpretation as a prior).
Notes that this claim rests on IF underperforming full S³martCirc.

items.question: If FI turned out to carry no information about nodes' behaviour, which interpretation of the RQ3 k-sweep would lose its basis?
items.answer: The interpretation that additional classification steps refine node identification. The paper reads the gain from −71% at k = 2 to about −96% at k = 6, and the rise in recovery, as better role-driven refinement. More steps on an uninformative FI signal would give no reason for such gains.
rubric: Identifies the RQ3 reading that more classification steps improve node identification and circuit quality.
Explains that this attribution presupposes FI provides a meaningful signal.

items.question: If S³martCirc's runtimes had been on the order of Act.'s (tens to hundreds of thousands of seconds), which claims would lose support, and which would remain intact?
items.answer: The efficiency claim (Table 2) and the conclusion's description of the method as advancing scalable MI would lose support. The Table 1 effectiveness and RQ2 recovery results would be unaffected.
rubric: Identifies the efficiency/scalability claim as undermined.
Notes that the accuracy-drop and recovery results do not depend on runtime.

items.question: If Act. had recovered a much larger share of Wang et al.'s IOI circuit than S³martCirc at every threshold, which RQ2 argument would weaken?
items.answer: The claim that S³martCirc aligns closely with human-verified mechanisms (recovery 'comparable only to Act.') would weaken. So would the argument that this alignment lends its circuits credibility on models without ground truth, such as Llama and Qwen.
rubric: Identifies the claim that S³martCirc's IOI recovery is top-tier (comparable to Act.)/aligned with human-verified circuits.
Notes the knock-on weakening of the credibility argument for settings without ground truth.

items.question: The appendix does not list k. Which k values is the Table 1 GPT-2 IOI result (−95.99%) consistent with, given RQ3?
items.answer: k = 6 or higher. RQ3 shows about −96% from k = 6 onward but only −71% at k = 2. The listed alpha of 0.75 also matches the best value in the sweep.
rubric: States k ≥ 6 (not small k such as 2).
Cites the sweep: −71% at k = 2 versus about −96% from k = 6, matching −95.99%.

items.question: Does Table 1 provide an independent measure of run-to-run variability for the Logit. metric? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. In every row the Logit. standard deviation is identical to the Acc. standard deviation, for example ±38.33 for Act. on GPT-2 Acronym and ±0.00 for S³martCirc on Qwen. This suggests the Logit. variability was not reported separately.
rubric: Answers not settled (or that the table does not give trustworthy logit variability).
Notes that each Logit. std equals the Acc. std in the same row.

items.question: Does the paper establish what varied between its three runs per setting? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The appendix states that all experiments used random seed 42, yet Table 1 reports nonzero standard deviations over three runs. The source of the run-to-run variation is never specified.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Points to the fixed seed 42 alongside nonzero standard deviations across three runs.

items.question: Does Table 2 confirm that the single Act. run on Qwen IOI fit within the stated 48-hour time limit? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. 187,663.88 s is about 52 hours, which exceeds 48 hours (172,800 s). The Qwen Acronym run, at about 168,689 s or 46.9 hours, does fit.
rubric: Answers contradicted.
Converts 187,663.88 s to about 52 h (or compares with 172,800 s), which exceeds 48 h.

items.question: Does the paper show that a larger sparsity coefficient yields smaller S³martCirc circuits? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The sparsity coefficient is never swept, and it varies together with model, task, learning rate and epochs. Across settings the pattern is not even monotone: Qwen Acronym (0.7) produced 12 nodes while Llama Acronym (1.0) produced 47.33.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Notes there is no sweep and the coefficient is confounded with other settings, e.g., Qwen 0.7 → 12 nodes versus Llama 1.0 → 47.33.

items.question: Does the 50% Acronym recovery show that S³martCirc's GPT-2 Acronym circuit consists mostly of known-circuit nodes? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. Recovery measures recall: 4 of the 8 known nodes were found. S³martCirc's GPT-2 Acronym circuits average about 60 nodes, so the large majority of their nodes lie outside the known 8-node circuit.
rubric: Answers contradicted (or that it does not show this).
Reasons that only 4 known nodes were recovered while the circuit has about 60 nodes, so recovery is recall, not precision.

items.question: Does the paper show that S³martCirc recovers more of Wang et al.'s IOI circuit than Act. does? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper describes S³martCirc's recovery as comparable only to Act. It claims superiority only over the other baselines, especially the optimization-based ones.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Notes that the paper calls the recovery 'comparable' to Act. rather than higher.

items.question: Does the paper show that increasing k never hurts S³martCirc? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The sweep covers only k up to 10 and only GPT-2 IOI. Accuracy stops improving after k = 6, so behaviour at larger k and in other settings is untested.
rubric: Answers not settled.
Notes the sweep is limited to k ≤ 10 on GPT-2 IOI only, with a plateau after 6.

items.question: RQ1 explains Act.'s weaker results by noting that patching-based methods evaluate nodes independently. Under what kind of circuit structure would Act.'s node scores fail most badly, and why?
items.answer: Act. would fail most badly when several nodes back each other up or jointly implement a step. Patching any one of them alone barely changes the logit difference because the others compensate, so each gets a low score. A jointly optimized mask can remove the whole group at once and reveal its importance.
rubric: Identifies redundant, compensating or jointly interacting nodes (e.g., backup heads) as the failure case
Explains that ablating one such node in isolation produces little logit-difference change, so each is scored as unimportant, while a joint mask can capture the group's effect

items.question: When could comparing Circuit Size across methods in Table 1 be misleading about how much model computation each circuit contains, and why?
items.answer: It is misleading when circuits differ in their mix of node types. The node set includes whole attention heads and individual feedforward neurons (d_n = 1), and each counts as one node. A circuit made mostly of single neurons and an equally sized circuit made of heads therefore contain very different amounts of computation.
rubric: States that size comparisons mislead when circuits differ in their mix of attention heads and feedforward neurons
Explains that Circuit Size counts each head and each single neuron (d_n = 1) as one node, so equal counts can represent very different amounts of computation

items.question: When would a high percent-recovered value in Figure 3 fail to show that a method's circuit is a precise description of the IOI mechanism, and why?
items.answer: It fails whenever the circuit also contains many nodes outside Wang et al.'s circuit. The metric counts the fraction of known-circuit nodes that appear in the discovered circuit, so extra irrelevant nodes are never penalized. This matters most at large thresholds such as 150–200 nodes.
rubric: States that high recovery can coexist with many extraneous, non-ground-truth nodes, especially at large thresholds
Explains that the metric measures coverage of the known circuit (recall) and does not penalize extra nodes (no precision component)

items.question: When could ablating a circuit produce a large Logit. drop but almost no Acc. drop, and why?
items.answer: This happens when ablation lowers the logit of the original predicted answer but competing tokens' logits fall by a similar amount. The predicted token then stays the argmax. Logit. tracks the raw logit of one token, while accuracy depends only on which token ranks first.
rubric: States that this happens when the answer's logit falls while competing logits fall comparably (or the answer stays top-ranked)
Explains that Logit. measures the raw logit of the original predicted answer, whereas accuracy depends only on the argmax ranking

items.question: Would S³martCirc's GPT-2 IOI advantage over Act. in Table 1 survive if S³martCirc were run with k = 2, and why?
items.answer: Essentially no. RQ3 reports about −71% accuracy drop at k = 2, which roughly ties Act.'s −70.71% (±25.89). The clear margin depends on using enough classification steps, around k = 6 (about −96%).
rubric: Concludes the advantage would largely vanish, leaving roughly a tie with Act.
Cites about −71% at k = 2 versus Act.'s −70.71%, compared with about −96% at k = 6

items.question: When would Attr.'s estimate of a node's contribution be unreliable compared with Act.'s direct patching, and why?
items.answer: It is unreliable when the logit-based metric responds nonlinearly as the node's activation moves from clean to corrupted. Attr. multiplies the activation difference by a single gradient, which is only a linear approximation of the patching effect. Attr. IG addresses this by integrating gradients along the path between the two activations.
rubric: Identifies a nonlinear relationship between the node's activation and the metric, or a large clean–corrupted difference, as the failure condition
Explains that Attr. uses a single-gradient linear approximation of the patching effect (which is why Attr. IG integrates along the path)

items.question: Why does the Acronym data generator keep only abbreviations whose three-letter concatenation tokenizes into exactly three tokens?
items.answer: The prompt ends with '(AB', and the model must predict the third letter. If each letter is its own token, the prompt ends at a token boundary and the answer C is a single token. The ground-truth y used in the cross-entropy term and in accuracy is a single vocabulary token, so this is required.
rubric: States that the filter ensures each letter is a separate token, so the target letter C is a single next token after '(AB'
Links this to the objective and evaluation using a single ground-truth token y in the vocabulary

items.question: S³martCirc is trained to make the model, with unimportant nodes masked out, reproduce the original output. Yet it is evaluated by ablating the circuit nodes. Why does the training objective nonetheless yield circuits whose ablation sharply hurts accuracy?
items.answer: L_disc forces the retained nodes alone to carry the computation that reproduces the model's output and the correct answer. The sparsity term keeps that retained set small. The task computation is therefore concentrated in the circuit nodes, so removing them at evaluation removes the mechanism.
rubric: Explains that training forces the few retained (circuit) nodes to carry the task computation needed to match P_orig and predict y
Notes that sparsity concentrates this computation in a small set, so ablating that set at evaluation destroys task performance

items.question: S³martCirc on Llama Acronym and on Qwen Acronym uses the same 50 epochs, 5 warmup epochs and learning rate. Why does the Qwen run take nearly twice as long (982.16 s vs 507.67 s)?
items.answer: The training schedule is the same, so the difference comes from the model. Qwen 3 1.7B is larger than Llama 3.2 1B, so it has more nodes, and therefore more masking coefficients, and each forward and backward pass costs more.
rubric: States that the difference comes from model size, since the schedule is identical
Explains that the larger Qwen model has more nodes/coefficients and costlier forward/backward passes per step

items.question: S³martCirc's Qwen accuracy drops are −100.00 ± 0.00 on both tasks. Why is the zero standard deviation not evidence that the three runs found the same circuit?
items.answer: An accuracy drop cannot exceed −100%, so every run that fully breaks the task scores the same. The circuit sizes do vary across runs (12 ± 1.63 and 16.33 ± 4.50), so the runs differ. The zero spread is a ceiling effect.
rubric: Identifies a ceiling effect: the drop is capped at −100%, so any run that fully breaks the task scores identically
Points to the nonzero spread in circuit size (±1.63, ±4.50) as showing the circuits differ across runs

items.question: To illustrate its comparable-circuit-size argument on Llama IOI, why does the paper contrast S³martCirc with Attr. IG rather than with the runner-up, Act.?
items.answer: Act. found a smaller circuit (13 nodes) with a sizeable −59.17% drop, so it would not show S³martCirc achieving more with fewer or equal nodes. Attr. IG uses more nodes (47.67) yet gets only −5.67%. That makes it a clean example of a larger circuit with far less effect.
rubric: Notes that Act.'s Llama IOI circuit is smaller (13 vs 35 nodes) with a substantial drop (−59.17%), so it would not support the argument
Notes that Attr. IG is larger (47.67) with a tiny drop (−5.67%), which cleanly supports it

items.question: In RQ3, why can percent circuit recovery keep rising with k beyond k = 6 while the accuracy drop stops improving?
items.answer: At k = 6 the accuracy drop is already about −96%, close to the −100% ceiling, so there is little room left to improve. Recovery measures overlap with Wang et al.'s circuit and is not near its maximum. Extra classification steps can therefore keep refining which nodes are selected toward the known circuit without changing the ablation effect.
rubric: Notes that accuracy drop is near its −100% ceiling (about −96%) at k = 6, so it saturates
Explains that recovery measures overlap with the known circuit and can keep improving as additional classification steps refine node selection

rubric: Answers yes

items.question: A team suspects their task is implemented partly by backup heads that take over when a primary head is removed. Based on the paper's RQ1 reasoning, should they prefer Act. or a mask-optimization method like S³martCirc, and why?
items.answer: They should prefer S³martCirc. The paper attributes patching's weakness to evaluating nodes independently, which misses interactions. With backup heads, ablating one head alone barely changes the output, whereas a jointly optimized mask can capture the group.
rubric: Recommends S³martCirc (joint mask optimization) over Act.
Explains that Act. scores nodes one at a time, so compensating backup heads each look unimportant, while a joint mask captures their interaction

items.question: A new circuit paper calls a head a 'mover' head. Should an S³martCirc user expect that head to be labelled passthrough, and why?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under Figure 1, name mover, negative name mover and letter mover heads all map to functional, because they transform information to amplify specific outputs. The role depends on how a node processes information, not on whether its name suggests moving information.
rubric: Says no, a 'mover' head need not be passthrough and may well be functional
Cites Figure 1 mapping name/letter mover heads to functional, since roles reflect how a node transforms information rather than the role's name or content

items.question: A team needs a GPT-2 circuit-discovery method whose accuracy-drop results are consistent from run to run. Between Act. and S³martCirc, which do the Table 1 results favour, and why?
items.answer: They favour S³martCirc. Its standard deviations are ±1.08 on Acronym and ±2.85 on IOI, compared with Act.'s ±38.33 and ±25.89.
rubric: Chooses S³martCirc
Cites S³martCirc's much smaller standard deviations on GPT-2 (±1.08/±2.85) versus Act.'s (±38.33/±25.89)

items.question: A team wants to intervene on the GPT-2 Acronym head, among S³martCirc's recovered nodes, that most directly shapes which output letter is emphasized. Should they target head 1.0 or head 11.4, and why?
items.answer: They should target head 11.4. S³martCirc classifies it as functional, matching its Letter Mover role, and functional nodes transform information to emphasize the correct output. Head 1.0 is a passthrough Previous Token head that only relays information.
rubric: Chooses head 11.4
Explains that 11.4 is functional (Letter Mover), which transforms information to emphasize the output, whereas 1.0 is passthrough (Previous Token) and only relays information

items.question: Two S³martCirc runs on Qwen IOI both give −100% accuracy drop, one with 12 nodes and one with 21 nodes. Given the paper's stated evaluation goal, which circuit should the team report, and why?
items.answer: They should report the 12-node circuit. The paper's goal is a minimal circuit that achieves maximal accuracy drop, and both circuits reach the maximal drop.
rubric: Chooses the 12-node circuit
Cites the goal of a minimal circuit with maximal accuracy drop, given that the drops are equal

items.question: A team scaling up to models larger than Qwen 3 1.7B must choose between IBCircuit and S³martCirc. Based on Tables 1 and 2, which should they choose, and why?
items.answer: They should choose S³martCirc. Its runtime grows more slowly with model size than IBCircuit's: on IOI it goes from about 264 s to 1048 s from GPT-2 to Qwen, while IBCircuit goes from about 467 s to 5153 s. IBCircuit also produced empty or zero-accuracy-drop circuits in every setting, whereas S³martCirc produced large drops.
rubric: Chooses S³martCirc
Cites that IBCircuit's runtime grows faster with model size (roughly 11x vs 4x from GPT-2 to Qwen on IOI)
Cites that IBCircuit gave empty or 0% accuracy-drop circuits

items.question: If prior work had found that circuit components are generally not reused across tasks with consistent roles, which part of the paper's argument would lose external support?
items.answer: The premise of c1 would lose external support. The paper cites component reuse with consistent roles (Merullo et al.) as evidence that a small set of computational roles recurs across tasks. That recurrence is what motivates a task-agnostic passthrough/functional dichotomy. The Figure 1 mapping of IOI and Acronym would remain, but only as two examples.
rubric: Identifies the claim that computational roles recur across tasks, motivating the task-agnostic dichotomy (c1)
Notes that the paper cites cross-task component reuse with consistent roles as support for this, leaving only the two-task Figure 1 mapping

items.question: Of the four recovered Acronym nodes, which ones give an unambiguous test of S³martCirc's role labels? If one of them had not been recovered, how would the RQ2 role evidence be affected?
items.answer: Only heads 1.0 (Previous Token, so passthrough) and 11.4 (Letter Mover, so functional) give unambiguous tests. Heads 8.11 and 10.10 can act as either Bridge or Letter Mover, so either label is defensible for them. Losing 1.0 or 11.4 would leave the claim that roles match Figure 1 resting on a single node.
rubric: Identifies 1.0 and 11.4 as the only unambiguous checks, because 8.11 and 10.10 can play either role
States that losing either would leave the role-agreement claim resting on a single node

items.question: If the alpha sweep had shown alpha = 0.0 (cross-entropy only) performing best on GPT-2 IOI, which RQ3 interpretation would fail?
items.answer: The interpretation that, for IOI, the KL faithfulness objective should be weighted more heavily than the task loss would fail. That conclusion rests on alpha = 0.75 being best. The claim that the cross-entropy term matters would still stand.
rubric: Identifies the conclusion that KL should be weighted more heavily than cross-entropy for IOI
Notes this rests on alpha = 0.75 being best, while the importance of the cross-entropy term would survive

items.question: If GPT-2's IOI name mover heads turned out to have FI below 1, what would that imply for the paper's claim that FI quantifies the functional/passthrough dichotomy?
items.answer: L_class would push these heads toward passthrough, because for FI < 1 the 1/FI term outweighs FI. Figure 1 maps name movers to functional. FI would then contradict the dichotomy it is meant to quantify, weakening c2's claim that FI assigns the roles of c1.
rubric: States that with FI < 1, L_class favours passthrough for these heads
Notes this contradicts Figure 1's mapping of name movers to functional, undermining FI as a quantification of the dichotomy

items.question: Suppose S³martCirc's Llama and Qwen circuits had produced Random-level accuracy drops, while its GPT-2 results were unchanged. Which claim would lose its support?
items.answer: The claim that S³martCirc generalizes across architectures would lose its support. The paper includes Llama 3.2 1B and Qwen 3 1.7B specifically to test this, and c4 asserts superiority across all three models. The GPT-2 evidence would remain.
rubric: Identifies the cross-architecture generalization claim (superiority across GPT-2, Llama and Qwen)
Notes that Llama and Qwen were included specifically to test generalization, so GPT-2-only success would not support it

items.question: If patching baselines had been rerun with joint multi-node ablations and still performed as poorly as in Table 1, which RQ1 explanation would lose its support?
items.answer: The explanation that patching-based methods underperform because they evaluate nodes independently and miss interactions would lose its support. Their weakness would then have to come from something else.
rubric: Identifies the explanation that patching evaluates nodes independently and misses interactions
Explains that joint ablations remove that limitation, so persistent failure would point to another cause

items.question: Does the paper show that Attr. IG's more accurate attribution yields more effective circuits than Attr.? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted as a general claim. Attr. IG beats Attr. on GPT-2 Acronym (−2.00 vs −0.17) and Llama IOI (−5.67 vs −1.50). Attr. is better on GPT-2 IOI (−12.73 vs −0.17) and Qwen IOI (−0.50 vs −0.33), and they tie on Qwen Acronym.
rubric: Answers contradicted (results are mixed rather than consistently favouring Attr. IG)
Cites at least one setting where Attr. beats Attr. IG (e.g., GPT-2 IOI −12.73 vs −0.17) alongside one where Attr. IG wins

items.question: Does the paper show that ablating S³martCirc's circuits nearly eliminates task accuracy on every model? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. The drops are near-total on GPT-2 (−97.50%, −95.99%) and Qwen (−100%). On Llama they are only −57.33% on Acronym and −69.00% ± 42.43 on IOI.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Cites the Llama drops (−57.33% Acronym, −69.00% IOI) as far from near-total elimination

items.question: Does Prune.'s 0% accuracy drop in Table 1 show that gradient-based edge pruning (Bhaskar et al.) is ineffective at circuit discovery? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The paper adapted Prune. to operate at the node level for a fair comparison. Its results therefore say nothing about the original edge-level method.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes that Prune. was adapted from edge-level to node-level pruning, so the results do not test the original edge method

items.question: Does the paper show that S³martCirc achieves its Table 1 results with a single hyperparameter configuration shared across models and tasks? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. Every model–task combination uses its own learning rate, epochs, warmup, sparsity coefficient and alpha, and no shared-configuration run is reported. RQ3 also shows that performance is sensitive to k and alpha.
rubric: Answers not settled (no shared-configuration experiment is reported)
Notes that hyperparameters are tuned per setting and that RQ3 shows sensitivity to k and alpha

items.question: Does Table 1 show that, on GPT-2, S³martCirc achieves a larger accuracy drop than Act. at matched circuit size? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. On GPT-2, S³martCirc's circuits are nearly twice Act.'s size (60.33 vs 35.00 on Acronym, 76.00 vs 39.33 on IOI). No size-matched accuracy comparison is reported, so part of its advantage could come from ablating more nodes.
rubric: Answers not settled
Cites S³martCirc's much larger GPT-2 circuits versus Act.'s and the absence of a size-matched accuracy comparison

items.question: Does the paper's text establish that removing the KL term (alpha = 0.0) degrades GPT-2 IOI performance as sharply as removing the cross-entropy term (alpha = 1.0)? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Not settled. The text reports only that alpha = 0.75 is best and that performance degrades sharply at alpha = 1.0. It does not describe how severe the drop is at alpha = 0.0.
rubric: Answers not settled
Notes the text describes only alpha = 0.75 being best and a sharp degradation at alpha = 1.0, with no characterization of alpha = 0.0

items.question: Does Circuit Size in Table 1 equal the number of nodes each method selected as important? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Contradicted. After a method selects nodes, any nodes not connected to the input or output are removed. Circuit Size counts only the remaining end-to-end connected circuit, which can be smaller than the selection or even empty.
rubric: Answers contradicted
Explains that disconnected nodes are removed and only the end-to-end connected circuit is counted

items.question: Does Table 1 show that S³martCirc achieves the largest Logit. drop in every model–task setting? Answer supported, contradicted or not settled, and why.
items.answer: Supported, in terms of reported means. S³martCirc has the largest Logit. drop in all six settings, though the margin on Llama IOI is small (−2.96 vs −2.37 for Act.) and the spread there is very large (±42.43).
rubric: Answers supported (S³martCirc has the largest mean Logit. drop in all six settings)
Notes the caveat that the Llama IOI margin over Act. is small (−2.96 vs −2.37) relative to its large standard deviation
